ai_technology: Linear support vector machine and linear discriminant analysis

evidence.ai_role: Learned linear classifiers test whether recorded population spike patterns distinguish stimulus conditions; direct spike-statistic findings are separate.
evidence.tested: Retrospective decoding of existing recordings: 33-mouse subset, balanced 100 ms windows, leave-one-out templates and fold-scaled linear SVM/LDA robustness checks.
evidence.unknown: Within-mouse window validation may retain block/session dependencies; no between-mouse generalization or behavioral hearing benefit. Nonsignificant age/strain differences do not prove equivalence.

source_review.scope: Primary full manuscript Methods, Results, validation protocol and limitations independently reviewed.

summary: A preprint reanalyzed auditory-cortex recordings and tested whether population activity distinguished silence, natural sounds and noise. In 33 mice with all three conditions recorded, a linear SVM achieved 82.50±8.74% mean accuracy using held-out time windows; template and linear-discriminant decoders gave similar results. Decoding remained above chance in both hearing-loss-prone and hearing-preserving strains across age groups, despite changes in individual-neuron activity. This does not establish intact perception, equivalence across ages or generalization to new mice; conditions were recorded in separate blocks.
title: Linear decoding distinguishes sound conditions in aging mouse cortex
